comparisons.peer_topic: General Trade and Export Regulatory Risks
comparisons.peer_summary: Export regulations, tariffs, and trade protection measures limit the ability to export products and may result in lost sales or material adverse effects. Compliance with ITAR and EAR is required, and failures or inability to obtain licenses could lead to penalties, loss of privileges, or difficulties in forecasting shipments.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies face regulatory risks that can materially affect their business, but the nature of the risk differs. QCOM focuses on legal challenges and litigation potentially forcing R&D cuts, while AMD focuses on trade disruptions, tariffs, and export controls limiting sales and impacting R&D execution. AMD specifically mentions that export control restrictions may impact the ability of R&D teams to execute product roadmaps, which parallels QCOM's concern about impairing technology leadership, but AMD's driver is external trade policy rather than general legal liability.

sentences.text: The occurrence of any of the above could have a material adverse effect on our business, revenues, results of operations, cash flows and financial condition, and our stock price could decline, possibly significantly, in which case we may have to significantly cut costs and other uses of cash, including in research and development, significantly impairing our ability to maintain product and technology leadership and invest in next generation technologies.

New export control restrictions may adversely impact the ability of our research and development teams located outside of the United States from executing our product roadmaps in a timely manner or at all.

comparisons.peer_summary: Legal, regulatory, and administrative investigations and claims arising from ordinary business conduct or otherwise could have a material adverse effect on the company's business, results of operations, or financial condition.
comparisons.comparison: Both QCOM and MU disclose that legal proceedings and investigations can have a material adverse effect on their business, results of operations, and financial condition. However, QCOM provides specific detail on the operational consequences, noting that such risks may force significant cuts in R&D and impair technology leadership, whereas MU's disclosure is a general statement without detailing specific operational impacts like R&D cuts.

comparisons.peer_topic: Indebtedness impact on financial position and strategy
comparisons.peer_summary: NVIDIA's substantial indebtedness may adversely affect its financial position, cash flows, and ability to implement its strategy or fulfill contractual obligations, potentially limiting flexibility and impairing future financing abilities.
comparisons.comparison: Both QCOM and NVDA identify indebtedness as a risk that can impact their ability to fulfill obligations and maintain financial flexibility. QCOM explicitly states that severe legal or adverse circumstances may impact the ability to timely pay indebtedness, while NVDA notes that its substantial indebtedness could prevent it from fulfilling contractual obligations. Both link financial strain (whether from legal costs or existing debt) to the inability to meet financial commitments.

sentences.text: Further, depending on the breadth and severity of the circumstances above, we may have to reduce, suspend or eliminate our capital return programs, and our ability to timely pay our indebtedness may be impacted.

The occurrence of any of the above could have a material adverse effect on our business, revenues, results of operations, cash flows and financial condition, and our stock price could decline, possibly significantly, in which case we may have to significantly cut costs and other uses of cash, including in research and development, significantly impairing our ability to maintain product and technology leadership and invest in next generation technologies.
Our indebtedness could adversely affect our financial position and cash flows from operations, and prevent us from implementing our strategy or fulfilling our contractual obligations.
